ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: the figure is a schematic diagram of an organic reaction transition state, with multiple curved arrows present; the problem requires ignoring these arrows. On the right side of the structure, an acetyl fragment CH3-C(=O)- can be seen, connected through an oxygen atom to another carbonyl, forming an acylated carboxyl/anhydride-like connection of CH3-C(=O)-O-C(=O)-. On the left side, an amide fragment R-C(=O)-NH- can be seen, and it is connected to the adjacent carbon skeleton; this adjacent carbon also bears a hydroxymethyl -CH2OH substituent. Reasoning: after ignoring the curved arrows, encoding from the right-side acetyl group starts as O=C(C)O-; continuing to connect to the adjacent carbonyl gives O=C(C)OC(=O)-; the α carbon connected to this carbonyl bears two substituents, NC(=O)R and CO (namely -CH2OH), so the overall SMILES is O=C(C)OC(=O)C(NC(=O)R)CO.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First describe the drawn structure while ignoring all curved arrows. Trace the main acylated carboxyl fragment from the right acetyl group: CH3-C(=O)-O-C(=O)-. Continue to the adjacent alpha carbon, which has two substituents: an amide nitrogen substituent N-C(=O)-R and a hydroxymethyl substituent -CH2OH. Encode this connectivity in SMILES as an acetyl ester of the amino-hydroxy acid skeleton: O=C(C)OC(=O)C(NC(=O)R)CO.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是一个有机反应过渡态示意图，存在多个弯箭头；题目要求忽略这些箭头。结构右侧可见一个乙酰基片段 CH3-C(=O)-，通过一个氧原子连接到另一个羰基，形成 CH3-C(=O)-O-C(=O)- 的酰化羧基/酸酐样连接。左侧可见酰胺片段 R-C(=O)-NH-，并连接到相邻的碳骨架；该相邻碳还带有羟甲基 -CH2OH 取代基。推理：忽略弯箭头后，从右侧乙酰基开始编码为 O=C(C)O-；继续接到相邻羰基得到 O=C(C)OC(=O)-；该羰基连接的α碳带有 NC(=O)R 和 CO（即 -CH2OH）两个取代基，因此整体 SMILES 为 O=C(C)OC(=O)C(NC(=O)R)CO。

planner_metadata.image_role: Use the image to identify the non-arrow molecular skeleton: a left amide fragment R/R1-C(=O)-NH attached to the alpha carbon; that carbon also bears a CH2OH side chain and a carbonyl group; the carbonyl is connected through an oxygen to an acetyl carbonyl group, giving an acyl-oxy/acyl ester linkage. planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to know the required output format is a SMILES expression and that reaction arrows in the transition-state diagram should be disregarded.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply standard line-angle interpretation and SMILES construction rules: unlabeled vertices are carbons with implicit hydrogens, labeled O/N atoms are heteroatoms, double lines indicate carbonyls, branches in SMILES represent substituents, and the generic R1 group can be represented as R in the target expression.
